messages: Nights 1-3: set up her room as the goal but start where she is. Make her bed inviting, same bedtime routine every night (bath, two books, lights low), and this stretch just move her sleep spot to a mattress or her bed inside your room, or sit beside her bed in her own room. At 2 she does best with a clear script: "you sleep in your bed now, I'll stay till you're settled." Expect protests and a couple of rough nights - that's normal, not a setback.

Nights 4-7: she sleeps in her own room. Do the same routine, tuck her in drowsy but awake, then sit by the bed without picking her up or chatting. Each night move your chair a little toward the door. When she gets up, walk her back calmly and quietly every time, no lecture - it can take a dozen returns the first night and far fewer by night four. A comfort item and a small night light both help toddlers feel safe.

After that: most families see it settle in about a week to two once the room and routine hold steady. You'll know it's working when returns drop and she wakes and stays put. If she gets up, keep the same calm walk-back rather than bringing her to your bed even once, since that resets the pattern. If she's still waking in real distress most nights after two weeks, or the resistance seems tied to fear or pain, worth raising with your doctor.
